calendar.impact: The API reported crude down 4.93 Mbbl and distillates down 2.6 Mbbl for the week ending Oct 16; the Reuters poll expects crude down 0.8 and distillates down 1.4. Production should rebound mechanically after the hurricane shut-in week (13,679 kb/d in the last print). The distillate line arbitrates the diesel crack's Tuesday close at $105.06.
calendar.title: EIA weekly report, week ending Oct 16 (08:30 MDT)

calendar.impact: Proposals for the Oct 16 re-offer of up to 17 Mbbl are due at 11:00 a.m. CT. A taken re-offer extends the exchange program on premium terms; a passed one says the premium structure is the binding constraint. No award has been published for the Sep 29 40 Mbbl round; posted contracts stand at 133.56 Mbbl to 13 companies.
calendar.title: SPR re-offer proposal deadline (11:00 a.m. CT)

calendar.impact: The November SYN tenor has rolled out of the ICE settlements file; Dec26 settled at +$5.55 on Oct 20 on zero volume. The pre-registered lines are +$7.00 (premium was priced for the return, or the return slipped) and +$6.50 (supply-return read confirmed); a scoring settle needs traded volume, and a zero-volume settle extends the window. The COT vintage as of Oct 20 is the first that can show whether Friday's escalation buying was short covering or new length, and the Week 43 Baltic weekly confirms or reverses the freight peak.
calendar.title: Syncrude return verdict (SYN), next COT vintage, Baltic Week 43

calendar.impact: The DNR's formal Notice of Violation of Oct 13 reaches its enforcement conference. Line 5 is operating via its temporary bypass; the conference is a regulatory-track event for the reroute, not a flow event today. Egypt's parliament also votes on authorizing support for Saudi Arabia.
calendar.title: Line 5 enforcement conference (Wisconsin DNR)

calendar.impact: The first of the Canadian majors to report the quarter that contains the fall turnaround windows. Upstream volumes are the first public test of whether Syncrude, Horizon and the Suncor plants returned on their guided schedules; no completion notices have been published for any of them.
calendar.title: Imperial Oil Q3 results

calendar.impact: The roll of November targets was the consensus at the last meeting, and the standing pause held through October with no delegate news ahead of the meeting. Any change in the production path lands directly on the global balance framing.
calendar.title: OPEC+ meeting

calendar.impact: December's Mainline nowcast opens at naive persistence on November's print (Light 19 percent, Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert). No December judgment call is registered yet. Nominations close at 0700 MST.
calendar.title: December Mainline nominations close (NOS day)

changes.balance: A fifth of light nominations cut at Kerrobert is a physical statement, and the strip's first traded December settle agreed with it on volume. The judgment call beat persistence on depth, and both missed the light side, which is the blind spot December's persistence nowcast inherits.
changes.body: The November Mainline apportionment notice landed Tuesday, a day after its expected date: Light 19 percent and Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert, with further cuts at Cromer, Superior and Clearbrook, up from October's 8 and 4 percent. Persistence (carrying October forward) missed by 11 and 3 points, a depth MAE of 7.0; the judgment call registered ahead of the notice (12 percent lights, 8 percent heavies) missed by 7 and 1, a depth MAE of 4.0, direction right on both classes. The same day, December WCS settled on real volume for the first time in this episode: 569 lots at a wider level.
changes.conditional: A December print that keeps widening on volume -> nominations pressure is being priced into the winter strip, not just November. A December retrace on volume -> the print was the event and November's cut stays a one-month fact.
changes.delta: November apportionment: Light 19 percent / Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert (Enbridge notice, Oct 20). WCS Dec26 -$27.95 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 20), down $0.45 on 569 lots; ARV Dec26 -$19.00; ARV to TMW December spread +$8.95.
changes.source: Enbridge apportionment notice, Oct 20, 2026; ICE Report Center EOD, Oct 20, 2026
changes.title: November apportionment lands at 19 percent lights; December WCS trades wider on its first volume

changes.balance: The premium is rented, not owned: Brent made a five-month high and closed lower on a mediation discussion, then recovered overnight on a mine claim that names no vessel. The inventory draws are the firmer leg; today's EIA distillate line and the SPR bid deadline are evidence, and everything since Monday is positioning around evidence.
changes.body: Brent touched $111.99 intraday on Tuesday, its highest in five months, then settled down $0.76 at $108.79 after Iran's president discussed mediation efforts with Pakistan's army chief in Tehran; the expiring November WTI settled at $101.79 and December WTI at $97.82, the front month from today. Overnight Brent recovered to $110.38 and WTI December to $99.18 at 0350 GMT (Reuters). The Revolutionary Guards Navy said a supertanker struck a sea mine south of the Strait and caught fire; the vessel is unnamed and the strike unconfirmed, and LSEG warns attacks have expanded into the Gulf of Oman against the ship-to-ship transfer system. The API reported crude down 4.93 Mbbl and distillates down 2.6 Mbbl for the week ending Oct 16, and two Energy Department officials said they are working with world refiners to boost fuel output amid the diesel shortage.
changes.conditional: An EIA distillate draw matching the API -> the physical tightness is confirmed at the official print and the crack's $105.06 close has support. A build -> Tuesday's premium and the API read both fade. Saudi confirmation of any Monday claim -> the risk premium becomes a supply event.
changes.delta: Tuesday settles: Brent Dec26 $108.79 (-$0.76, intraday high $111.99, highest in five months); WTI Nov26 expiry $101.79 (-$1.87); WTI Dec26 $97.82. Overnight: Brent $110.38 (+1.5 percent), WTI Dec26 $99.18 (+1.4 percent) at 0350 GMT (Reuters). Diesel crack $105.06 on the completed Oct 20 close (validated history).
changes.source: Reuters, Oct 20 to 21, 2026 (Tuesday settles; overnight marks at 0350 GMT; mediation discussion; mine claim via Iranian media; LSEG Gulf of Oman warning; API via market sources)
changes.title: Brent round-trips a five-month high on mediation talk, recovers overnight on draws and a mine claim

changes.balance: Freight stays a headwind at record-extreme levels and the export arb stays closed, but the tightening impulse has reversed: the trapped-barrel pressure on Houston pricing now eases at the margin if Friday's weekly confirms the turn. The FOB discount gauge itself has not printed since late September, so the relief is unconfirmed in prices.
changes.body: The Baltic Week 42 weekly (Oct 16) shows the first broad pullback of the freight episode on every major route, and it carries the TD9 print this digest had been missing: TD9 (Caribbean to US Gulf Coast) at WS 830, down 198 points on the week, replacing the Oct 9 level of WS 1030 carried until now. TD3C eased to WS 1281.25, TD22 (US Gulf Coast to China) to an $80.58 million lumpsum, TD25 to WS 755. RBN's freight series opener, with McQuilling data, has the easing continuing past the weekly: the VLCC US Gulf Coast to Asia voyage at $65.39 million as of Oct 19 and the Aframax US Gulf Coast to Europe voyage at WS 648.89, off WS 1000 on Oct 6.
changes.conditional: A Week 43 weekly (Friday) extending the pullback -> the freight turn is real and the arb math starts to reopen at the margin. A snap back toward the records -> Week 42 was a pause in the tightening, not the peak.
changes.delta: Baltic Week 42 (Oct 16): TD9 WS 830 (-198 points); TD3C WS 1281.25, TCE $1,370,193 per day; TD22 $80.58 million lumpsum, TCE $559,334 per day; TD25 WS 755. RBN/McQuilling, Oct 19: VLCC USGC to Asia $65.39 million; Aframax USGC to Europe WS 648.89.
changes.source: Baltic Exchange weekly, Oct 16, 2026, via shipping-press republications; RBN Energy, Oct 21, 2026
changes.title: Freight peaked in Week 42: TD9 printed WS 830 and the easing extended into Oct 19

flags.body: Kpler puts confirmed Hormuz flows at a seven-day average of 10.17 Mb/d, 41 percent below the prewar baseline, with at least 18 vessels reportedly attacked over two weeks. The Revolutionary Guards Navy said Tuesday a supertanker struck a sea mine south of the Strait and caught fire; the vessel is unnamed and the strike is unconfirmed, and LSEG warns targeting has expanded into the Gulf of Oman against the ship-to-ship transfers that support loadings. The Houthis claimed Saudi Arabia's Yanbu terminal site, Shaybah field and two airports on Monday; Saudi authorities have not confirmed and the claims are unverified. Trade the flow prints and confirmed incidents, not the claims.
flags.title: Hormuz flows 41 percent below prewar; mine claim unnamed, attacks spreading to the Gulf of Oman
flags.trigger: Saudi confirmation of any Monday claim, a named vessel or independent confirmation for the mine claim, or a Kpler flow print stepping down again

flags.body: The Oct 16 executive order waived the Graham Act sanctions, restrictions and duties under the Section 115 national-interest waiver. The president defended the waiver on Monday while noting a final decision is still to be announced, and the Secretary of State cited up to 60 days to assess the impact. Still missing: a reported loading, a named buyer, and a shipment schedule, with Moscow's export ban running through October and Ryazan's CDU-6 suspended. On Tuesday two Energy Department officials said they are working with refiners worldwide to boost fuel output instead. The waiver raises the probability the barrels eventually move; it does not schedule them.
flags.title: Sanctions waiver: terms undecided, no cargo reported, DOE working the refiner channel
flags.trigger: A reported Russian diesel loading, a named buyer, or a move in Congress to block the arrangement

flags.body: November Mainline apportionment is Light 19 percent and Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert (Enbridge notice, Oct 20), up from October's 8 and 4 percent. WCS Dec26 settled at -$27.95 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 20), down $0.45 on 569 lots, the widest marker of the episode on its first traded volume. December's nowcast opens at persistence on November's levels; no December judgment call is registered yet, and December nominations close Nov 17.
flags.title: November apportionment at 19 percent lights; December traded wider on volume
flags.trigger: A December settle that retraces or extends on volume, or registration of a December judgment call ahead of the Nov 17 nominations close

flags.body: The Baltic Week 42 weekly (Oct 16) showed the first broad pullback of the freight episode: TD3C at WS 1281.25, TD22 (US Gulf Coast to China) TCE at $559,334 per day, TD25 at WS 755, and TD9 (Caribbean to US Gulf Coast) at WS 830, down 198 points from WS 1030. RBN/McQuilling data to Oct 19 shows the easing continuing (VLCC US Gulf Coast to Asia $65.39 million; Aframax to Europe WS 648.89). Levels remain record-extreme and the export arb stays closed. High Caribbean to Gulf freight makes competing heavy sellers captive to the Gulf, so their length is offered at deeper FOB discounts and pressures WCS Houston pricing whether it fills or not; that discount gauge has not printed since late September.
flags.title: Freight peaked in Week 42; the turn is unconfirmed until Week 43
flags.trigger: The Week 43 Baltic weekly on Friday, a fresh competing-grade FOB discount print, or a WCS Houston response to the freight turn
